summary: Implemented the Phase 6 entry boundary for library events. JellyfinLibraryEventSource now maps Jellyfin ItemChangeEventArgs synchronously and in memory to a bounded LibraryItemChangedEventArgs (item id, LibraryWorkReason, structural MediaItemType?, and LibraryItemChangeOrigin). LibraryEventRelevance validates relevance against the current public PluginConfigurationSnapshot with no I/O (an enabled Arr connection, a V1 badge-bearing Movie/Episode for add/update, and no image-only or ArrTags-generated internal update). Relevant changes become a bounded provider-neutral LibraryWorkHint (item id, reason, safe configuration version) and are enqueued through the narrow IWorkHintSink boundary; BoundedWorkHintSink is a thread-safe, QueueCapacity-bounded implementation that coalesces redundant hints, drops overflow, performs no external I/O, and never throws. ArrTagsLifecycleService uses one synchronous handler for added/updated/removed, contains unexpected exceptions so they never reach the host publisher, and preserves the task 5.9 ItemRemoved tracked/bounded drain/tombstone behavior while also emitting a removal hint. DI registers the sink lazily from OperationalLimits.QueueCapacity with no startup work. The full queue/worker policy (coalescing by connection, single-flight, cancellation, retry classification, overflow policy) remains task 6.2.

known_limitations: The handler drops every Jellyfin image-only update (ItemUpdateType.ImageUpdate) because the event boundary cannot distinguish an ArrTags-generated image publication from an external image change without an in-memory marker or an I/O read. A changed source image is therefore picked up by a later work item or by fingerprint-driven invalidation (task 6.6) rather than by this handler; this is documented in LibraryItemChangeOrigin and LibraryItemChangedEventArgs.

The bounded sink has no consumer in task 6.1: hints remain queued up to QueueCapacity and overflow is dropped until task 6.2 supplies the worker, coalescing-by-connection, single-flight, and cancellation policy.

Coalescing by connection, single-flight work, worker cancellation, retry classification, dynamic capacity changes, restart-safe draining, and the full queue-overflow policy are deliberately out of scope and remain task 6.2.
Only an in-process validation was performed; no live Jellyfin host was available, consistent with the pinned-host absence noted for the environment.
